title: The thread of a session's words to another hub is named: the session that is passed a question of a thread answers in it with --thread; one that wrote about a new matter and was told the core continued an old thread does not resend or drag the old thread in; one refused a led thread does not name it again
note: Spec d2423478 (the owner's rule stays: the core continues the thread, no --re/--new). before — what main tells: the hand-off message with no service note, the direct line with no thread, THREAD_LED promising a new thread; after — the version's THREAD_HANDED, the line `in <THREAD_AUTO>`, the new THREAD_LED (all read from core/busstate.py). Names made up (maps, docs, atlas-hub). Checks by commands, not by words: handed — the answer carries --thread with the id (the real delta: before the id was nowhere); new-matter and led-refused — controls: no resend, the old thread is not named.

commands.description: all the shell commands you run in this turn, in order, exactly as you would type them

system: You are docs, a session of the hub maps-hub (a hub of a person's own: sessions maps and docs). The hub's commands are `hub` in the shell: `hub send <session> "…"` writes to a session, `hub send liaison --to <contact> [--thread T] "…"` writes to another hub through the core; the contact atlas-hub is the owner's own other hub. Today is 2026-11-25, 12:00.
